story:
My whole life, my dad has wanted to go to Canada and hunt bears. In 2018 I decided to book a hunt for 2020. I spent a lot of time researching to find the right spot. I didn’t want to sit in a tree stand all day, and I didn’t want a big commercial outfit. I wanted a family-run operation.

I was watching an episode of Eastmans’ and saw Crystal Lake Resort in central BC. They were killing great bears, it looked like a family operation, and they hunted spot-and-stalk. It seemed perfect. My dad reluctantly said yes and we were ready to go.

Then COVID hit. Between the lockdowns and the government nonsense, we couldn’t go in 2020 or 2021. Finally, in 2022, we were on our way. We took the opportunity to make some stops since neither of us had ever been to Canada. The drive up was awesome.

Our goal was to kill two bears, spot-and-stalk, with a bow. We would be the first hunters into this area since 2019, and we were excited. We chose a full week in May to take advantage of the bears coming out of their dens.

The outfit was family-owned by Dan and Ellen Brooks. They have seven girls and grew up on that land. What an awesome family. Everything they did made us feel at home.

Because of COVID, the Brooks family had been renting the bear cabins to a mining company to stay afloat, so we stayed at the Happy Hands Ranch instead. Years earlier a Korean company had bought the property and tried to build a resort and hotel for Asian tourists. Long before we got there it had fallen apart. Dan had some amazing stories about the owner. They still owned the land and left a single worker to keep everything up. That’s where we stayed. It was kind of crazy. There was another family in camp that week, so we got to hunt with Cody. Early in life Cody had made a couple of young, dumb mistakes that got him a DUI. In Canada, that meant he lost the ability to own firearms.

Before we arrived, Dan and the neighboring guide had been in a bit of a feud. The first day we were hunting we ran into the other guide with an American hunting influencer from Nocked On. The guy was painted up in full camo and face paint, and they said they were headed into town. I don’t know many people who drive into town looking like that. After Dan and the other guide had a phone conversation, we went back to hunting.

There was a turnaround spot between the two zones that we had been using. That day a Fish and Game officer was waiting for us. He walked up to the window and said hi to Cody. Cody had never met the guy before, so it was clear the officer had been waiting specifically for us. He knew Cody wasn’t allowed to have a firearm and demanded Cody hand it over. Things got heated.As we were talking, Dan pulled up—he had been meeting with the other outfitter. Suddenly the officer asked for my rifle. I told him he’d have to pry it from my cold, dead American hands. That didn’t go well. I handed over my paperwork, but the officer didn’t care. He and Dan stood face-to-face screaming at each other. The officer finally admitted he shouldn’t have demanded my gun, but it was too late. The Mounties were on their way, and if there weren’t two guns when they arrived, we were all going to jail—him included.Dan told us to jump in the truck and left Cody to finish dealing with the officer. Boy, were spirits low.

We had seen a bunch of bears the first two days but never had a real opportunity. Dan took us to the far end of the unit, away from the officer, to hunt on a nice lady’s homestead where bears had been attacking the horses. We saw twelve bears that evening. With bows in hand we started several stalks. Nothing quite worked out.

As it got late, Dan asked if we would consider shooting one of the bigger bears with a rifle. With snow forecast for the rest of the hunt, we decided to change plans. Since my rifle was headed to jail, Dan went back to the truck to get his. While he was gone we tried a couple more times with the bows—so close, but not quite close enough.When Dan got back, he and my dad put a stalk on a beautiful black bear. Right before the stalk, Dan and I disagreed on which of the four bears in the field was bigger. They made a great stalk and Dad made a great shot on an awesome bear.

While we were talking about that bear, the one I thought was bigger walked back into the field. Dan looked at me and said, “How about a double?” I grabbed the rifle, settled over the shooting sticks, and one shot later had a dead bear. What had started as a tough day ended with two great bears.

The next day we went on a four-wheeler trip while Dan went into town to try to get my rifle back. By the end of the day the officer asked me to come into town to sign for it. After some heated words he apologized for taking my rifle (which he admitted was illegal on his part) and I signed the paper.This trip didn’t lack excitement. I’m so glad we went. We got to meet a great family and made some incredible memories..
